```python
def seed_partition(n, sigma, trans, accept):
    rev = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for q in range(n):
        row = trans[q]
        for c in range(sigma):
            t = row[c]
            if t != q: rev[t].append(q)
    dist = [-1]*n
    dq = deque()
    for q in range(n):
        if accept[q]:
            dist[q] = 0
            dq.append(q)
    while dq:
        u = dq.popleft()
        d = dist[u] + 1
        for p in rev[u]:
            if dist[p] < 0:
                dist[p] = d
                dq.append(p)
    order = {}
    part = [0]*n
    for q in range(n):
        d = dist[q]
        ident = order.get(d)
        if ident is None:
            ident = len(order); order[d] = ident
        part[q] = ident
    return part, len(order)
```
Note: self-loops (t == q) are skipped in rev — that's fine for BFS distances (a self-loop never shortens a distance). Careful: skipping self-loops is valid because if dist[q] is known, a self-loop adds nothing. ✓
